style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;margin-top: 0;">Hey folks,</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>It’s a heatwave in the UK, and I can’t think straight. Dan went on Lenny’s podcast to talk about agents, automation and SaaSpocalypse, which is </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/53f646f1-f9c8-4e7e-b178-9a0ab19edd95?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">worth checking out</a><span>. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">While I generally agree with it all, the one thing I can’t shake is the bullish case for SaaS. I think SaaS is in trouble…</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I don’t think it’s in trouble because you can build your own versions with a plan, patience and prompts. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">With SaaS tools, you pay monthly for a set of features and stability. The problem is that the tool needs to keep growing. They add new features, change the interface, do all sorts of things you may not need (and often hate).</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">The tool is for the masses but you may have only wanted a sliver. The tools can outgrow you and why you bought it in the first place.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">So if I only need a sliver, I’ll go looking for pieces I can pull together myself. A document editor over here, an agent there, etc. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I think SaaS companies that can unbundle their building blocks and sell them as composable pieces for users (as well as the all-in bundle) could be a very interesting bet. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>WorkOS do this well. Their tagline on Google results is literally “</span><em>WorkOS</em><span> is a set of building blocks for quickly adding enterprise features to your app”. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Stripe does this too. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">In the age of customisable software and using tools with agents, I can’t imagine paying for a tool that I can’t change its feel or features. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">It’s why I think API/CLI/SDK-first companies are in a really interesting place.</p><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: 0;height: 1px;background: rgb(0,0,0,.1);border: none;"></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em><span>Ben’s Bites is brought to you by </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/8c27cd0d-5197-4189-902a-035e54bdaa5b?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Sherlocq</a></em></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #ea580c;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/8c27cd0d-5197-4189-902a-035e54bdaa5b?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Sherlocq</a><span> is an AI-powered regulatory intelligence platform built for compliance, legal, and regulatory professionals. Research regulations, analyse documents, and run sanctions checks across 30+ jurisdictions and 320+ sanctions sources, </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/8c27cd0d-5197-4189-902a-035e54bdaa5b?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">cutting research time by up to 70%</a><span>.</span></p></blockquote><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: 0;height: 1px;background: rgb(0,0,0,.1);border: none;"></div><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.125em * 1);">Headlines</h4><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/54148cff-2ecf-42d4-9b49-44e95e0f6057?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Appshots in Codex</a></strong><span> attach the active Mac window to a Codex thread with a screenshot + available text, including context beyond what is visible. </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/54715f16-28fe-4557-895d-354833710d0d?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Goal mode</a><span> in Codex is now out of the experiment stage - Transcribe the video and pull out the keyframes linked to timestamps for important information. When the user is talking about something that is not dynamic, create short GIFs from the keyframes.</p></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Let me know any cool use-cases or remixes of this 😊 </p><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: 0;height: 1px;background: rgb(0,0,0,.1);border: none;"></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em><span>Ben’s Bites is brought to you by </span><strong><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/a6d42c1f-d5b6-468e-8cde-ce870ffdd395?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Hyperagent from Airtable</a></strong></em></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #ea580c;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/a6d42c1f-d5b6-468e-8cde-ce870ffdd395?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Hyperagent</a><span>, the cloud agent system with full computing environments, is giving $10M in inference credits to help founders build and run agent-first companies. item.title: Learn the system
item.author: ben's bites <bensbites@substack.com>
item.content:encoded:
<html lang="en" dir="ltr" style="scrollbar-width: thin;scrollbar-color: rgb(219,219,219)rgb(255,255,255);"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Learn the system</title><style>
@media (max-width: 1024px) {
  .typography .pullquote-align-left,
  .typography.editor .pullquote-align-left,
  .typography .pullquote-align-right,

    float: none;
    margin: 0 auto;
    width: 100%;
    max-width: 100%;
  }
}

  .typography .markup table.image-wrapper img,
  .typography.editor .markup table.image-wrapper img,
  .typography .markup table.kindle-wrapper img,
  .typography.editor .markup table.kindle-wrapper img {
    max-width: 550px;
  }
}
@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .typography:not(:has(#toc)) .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-left),
  .typography.editor:not(:has(#toc)) .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-left) {
    margin-left: var(--image-offset-margin);
  }
  .typography:not(:has(#toc)) .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-right),
  .typography.editor:not(:has(#toc)) .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-right) {
    margin-right: var(--image-offset-margin);
  }
}
@media (min-width: 1300px) {
  .typography .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-left),

    margin-left: var(--image-offset-margin);
  }
  .typography .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-right),
  .typography.editor .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-right) {
    margin-right: var(--image-offset-margin);
  }
}
@media (max-width: 1024px) {
  .typography,

    /* Disable offset on mobile/tablet */

  .typography .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-left),
  .typography.editor .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-left),

  .typography.editor .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-right) {

    margin: 1em auto;
    max-width: 100%;
    width: auto;
    padding: 0;
  }
  .typography .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-left.thefp),
  .typography.editor .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-left.thefp),

  .typography.editor .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-right.thefp) {
    margin: 1em auto;
  }
  .typography .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-left),
  .typography.editor .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-left),
  .typography .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-right),
  .typography.editor .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-offset-right) {
    margin: 1em auto;
  }
  .typography .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-left) .image2-inset,
  .typography.editor .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-left) .image2-inset,
  .typography .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-right) .image2-inset,
  .typography.editor .captioned-image-container figure:has(> a.image2-align-right) .image2-inset {
    display: block;
    justify-content: initial;
  }
}
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .typography .markup div.sponsorship-campaign-embed,

    margin-bottom: 24px;
  }

}

I’ve used Superhuman for years. I like it a lot. It is fast, keyboard-first, clean, and is good software. But like many saas products, it keeps adding features that I don’t need and more importantly, I don’t need to be paying for email.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I wanted a split inbox and rules to organize my emails.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Kicking off with Codex:</p><div class="callout-block" data-callout="true" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;background-color: rgb(238,238,238);border-radius: 8px;margin: 32px 0;padding: 16px 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;margin: 8px 0;">I’ve got an idea. Gmail should stay the source of truth.</p></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">The end product has split inboxes, shortcuts, command palette, The whole app is built on top of this.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Investigate why there is a delay with anything in this app. I want everything to feel instant.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">It found the app was pinging Gmail too much, too often.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">So it then started showing cached data immediately, refreshing in the background, prefetching thread details and updating the UI optimistically when I archive or label something.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>This is one of the reasons I like building with agents. bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);">Email rendering</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Showing email sounds easy until you try to show email.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Plain text, Gmail HTML, newsletters, receipts, calendar invites, inline images, signatures, quoted replies, tracking pixels, weird MIME stuff. Horrible little world.</p><div class="callout-block" data-callout="true" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;background-color: rgb(238,238,238);border-radius: 8px;margin: 32px 0;padding: 16px 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;margin: 8px 0;">The email renderer needs to handle all kinds of email and display them well. Normal human emails should feel native. Designed newsletters/receipts can render differently. Use good open-source libraries.</p></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Codex improved the system but with a bunch of specific rules like if this do that.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">So I stepped away and tried to think about other ways to approach it. I know Obsidian has a web clipper that displays nice previews of web pages. So I got Codex to reverse engineer the chrome extension to understand how it works.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">So then I asked to apply that approach to email rendering. It’s still not prefect and I’ve given up on perfect for now so normal emails look good (enough) and html heavy emails (like this newsletter, amazon, etc) just get shown as they are.</p><div So I got Factory to fix those and essentially hide that part of the email from the user.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Factory then found one of my favourite bugs. A normal email with a fancy signature rendered like a designed newsletter.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Why? Logo/table signature. The classifier thought the signature meant the whole email was a designed HTML email.</p><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);">Search and All Mail</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Then I added a search page for all my emails.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">And then, All Mail, because sometimes I do need to see what’s been archived.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">But it was a bit off…</p><div class="callout-block" data-callout="true" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;background-color: rgb(238,238,238);border-radius: 8px;margin: 32px 0;padding: 16px 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;margin: 8px 0;">Nah its funky as fuck. Use the browser to test it.</p></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">The fix was to lazy-load All Mail and stop hammering Gmail.</p><div 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);">My takeaways</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I don’t advise building an email client 😅.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">If you want a feature (and then another) just build it and see what feels right. Code is cheap.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Switch between tools (harnesses) and models.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Think about other tools or apps that may do all or parts of what you’re trying to do. Ask your agent to reverse engineer it.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Use fresh sessions outside of your project to get unbiased opinions on implementations. Your agent is influenced by everything in it’s context.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Ask the agent a lot of “I assumed it was doing this, is it?”, “Why does this happen?”, “Whats the best way to do this?”, “What are the tradeoffs of this approach?”</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Get agents to use the browser to test things out, a lot.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">You learn a lot from building for fun or for the sake of it. So just build stuff!</p><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: 0;height: 1px;background: rgb(0,0,0,.1);border: none;"></div><h3 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.375em * 1);">My stack</h3><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">So many tools. So little time. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Everyone feels the same - so just find tools you need for the job you need to complete. Don’t worry about all the new shiny tools every day.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Day-to-day ‘work’ i.e. brainstorming, talking about ideas, essentially everything non-coding heavy (like bigger projects or apps) I’m still using </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/8544bd2a-8d1b-4081-a4c4-0ff5c1e1c996?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Pi</a><span>, but now with GPT 5.5 since Anthropic has cracked down…boo! But I’m liking 5.5 - GPT models tend to follow instructions more directly so it really matters what you have in your AGENTS.md and context.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I’ve also spent the last 2 weeks in the Codex app - it’s really good. Use a VPN if in EU/UK so you can use the chrome and computer use tools. But I still find myself preferring the terminal (with Pi) because you can see everything the agent is doing and jump in to course-correct (or tweak your instructions). But IMO this app is better than the Claude variants. Don’t bother using Cowork - it’s limited and they’ll merge it into Claude Code soon enough - don’t be put off by ‘code’ in the name. All these coding agents are just great general agents. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>For ‘real’ coding i.e. when I’m serious about building something, I use </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/e77bdb7a-c334-4858-8d88-7319aa05d4d0?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Factory</a><span>. It’s the best harness for code, especially if you don’t know </span><em>how to actually</em><span> </span><em>code</em><span>. It’s more complete, and seems to handle everything much more than others I’ve used - plus you can switch between Claude and Opus models very easily. They recently launched a $100 plan too with better limits too. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>For full stack apps I’m sticking with Vercel, Stripe and Supabase. I just started using Stripe’s </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/5db2c018-f6df-45be-9da3-3875c282be9c?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">projects.dev</a><span> which will set up all three of those apps (and many others) all in one. Your agent can basically just use projects.dev, set up, manage and link all the other services you need to get apps setup properly. Super helpful as you don’t have to manually add or manage each yourself. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>I use </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/366f1435-1da8-402b-9aac-c6da896732c4?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">here.now</a><span> </span><strong>a lot</strong><span> - I’m always spinning up new sites for random ideas or tasks like visualising data and things of that nature. Plus sites are easier to read than pure documents. Just give the instructions (copy from the homepage) to your agent and you get free websites spun up on-demand. Super slick and easy. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>For document editing and writing I’ve been using </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/66e83cab-2f15-4bd4-9658-b8b2e24253a6?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Clearly</a><span> quite a lot recently. I like it - I don’t know what I really want out of a document editor like this, truly I just want to view and edit docs within whichever tool I’m using (pi/droid/codex) but none let you do all of that…yet. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>That’s mostly it - other than a bunch of CLI tools like </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/8672a2cd-dd03-4f8b-b79a-c431763de45e?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">downloading youtube videos</a><span> or podcasts, getting transcripts, and I use markdown.new for my agents to easily grab website information (It’s in my AGENTS.md so my agents use it - i.e. https://markdown.new/www.example.com - but I recently discovered defuddle.md which I may switch to).</span></p><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: how quick and nice it is to use. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I don’t need (…yet? ever?) AI to read all my emails, draft replies, chase me to do things and be a PA for me, I’ve had PA’s and I always let them go.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I just want email rules - if this address is labelled ‘pitch’ (for PR pitches), archive it. If no label - it’s ‘important’ and needs a reply for me, if ‘investing’ it’s from an LP or portfolio founder, if ‘newsletter’ archive it (don’t do this or you wont see these! 😊). </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Gmail has filters and labels but it’s limited and just can’t give me the UI I want to work in. So naturally, I built my own. I’ll send a ‘Ben’s Builds’ email on Saturday with more details on what I actually did. It took me ~2 hours for the first version.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>I was ‘pushed’ to this by seeing Dan Shipper’s </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/568cabb7-1636-41a9-b48b-c40306937b86?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Codex-native email workflow</a><span> - but again, I don’t need most of the stuff he’s doing. Email is very different for everyone. But now I can completely customise my experience…If I want daily briefs to summarise all my newsletters - my agent can do it, if I want automated actions - my agent can, and so on. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">So if you send me an email, it is me who will reply - but my agent may have you labelled and organised to make it easier for me to respond.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Personal software can be built by anyone!</p><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: 0;height: 1px;background: rgb(0,0,0,.1);border: none;"></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em><span>Ben’s Bites is brought to you by </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/1b314be7-ec8d-4329-8edf-203dce599499?j=eyJ1IjoiOGE4YmF5In0.KHS6HMDdHIBtymIGSuwpkS0DCXGklZtdBNsEExOOEHs" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Attio</a></em></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #ea580c;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">GTM Atlas is the map for modern go-to-market.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Written by top operators, Atlas is a free resource covering the full customer journey, with systems thinking that scales with you.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Curated by Attio.
